title: Cluster Topology and Sharding Strategies
description: Design effective Redis Cluster topologies and choose sharding strategies that match your workload patterns.

data.text: How you arrange your Redis Cluster topology and choose your sharding strategy directly impacts latency, throughput, and operational complexity. The right topology balances data distribution, fault tolerance, and query patterns.

Production Redis Cluster deployments typically use 3 or more master nodes, each with 1-2 replicas. The minimum viable production cluster is 3 masters with 1 replica each (6 total nodes). This ensures that losing any single node — master or replica — leaves the cluster fully operational.

data.title: Minimum Production Topology
data.text: Never deploy a Redis Cluster with fewer than 6 nodes (3 masters + 3 replicas) in production. With fewer nodes, a single failure can make the cluster unreachable.

data.caption: Recommended production Redis Cluster topology: 3 masters with 1 replica each
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    M1[Master 1]
    M2[Master 2]
    M3[Master 3]
    R1[Replica 1]
    R2[Replica 2]
    R3[Replica 3]
    APP[Application] --> M1
    APP --> M2
    APP --> M3

data.text: Redis Cluster uses key-based (hash-based) sharding by default. Range-based sharding (where contiguous keys are stored together) is sometimes used for range scans, but Redis Cluster does not support it natively. If your workload requires range queries, consider using a Redis Enterprise module like RedisJSON with indexing or a separate indexing layer.

cards.title: Hash-Based Sharding
cards.description: Keys are hashed to determine their slot. All keys are distributed uniformly.
cons: Multi-key ops limited to same slot

cards.title: Hash Tag Sharding
cards.description: Use {hash-tag} in key names to force related keys into the same slot.
cons: Can create hot spots if not designed carefully

cards.title: Range-Based Sharding
cards.description: Keys are grouped by value ranges into specific nodes.
cons: Not natively supported in Redis Cluster

data.text: Redis Cluster allows hash tags using curly braces: {user:1001}:profile and {user:1001}:sessions are stored in the same slot because only the substring inside braces is hashed. This enables atomic multi-key operations like pipelines and transactions on related keys.

data.title: Using Hash Tags with Redis Cluster and Node.js (ioredis)

items.text: Use at least 3 master nodes in production
items.hint: Fewer than 3 masters cannot tolerate any master failure

items.text: Deploy at least 1 replica per master
items.hint: Zero replicas means any master failure causes data loss

items.text: Plan for 30% headroom in memory per node
items.hint: Redis needs memory for replication, RDB snapshots, and overhead

items.text: Use hash tags for keys that need atomic multi-key operations
Avoid cross-slot multi-key commands like MSET across different hash tags

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Minimum production topology: 3 masters + 3 replicas (6 nodes)
Redis Cluster uses hash-based sharding into 16,384 slots
Hash tags ({...}) force related keys into the same slot for multi-key ops
Range-based sharding is not natively supported in Redis Cluster
data.takeaway: Design your cluster topology around your failure tolerance requirements, and use hash tags to group related data for atomic operations.
